result.title: AgentPolicyForge: From Executable Environments to Policy Benchmarks and Adaptive Guards
result.summary: Customized agent deployments define policies over tools, resources, and execution conditions. Providing these policies in the task agent's prompt does not reliably prevent violations. Training a guard requires examples of tool calls that comply with or violate those policies. We introduce AgentPolicyForge, a framework that uses executable environments to construct policy benchmarks and iteratively train policy guards. With this framework, we construct PolicyGym, a dataset across ten policy families using 698 scenarios for training data generation and 254 separate held-out scenarios for human-reviewed test sets. Tool calls are executed and their outcomes recorded to help determine whether they comply with the policy. Every violating case uses a permitted tool, requiring checks of arguments, resources, and context rather than tool identity alone. The case construction process supports iterative guard training: an attacker generates requests using retrieved strategies, and the guard is fine-tuned on balanced, environment-verified examples. Training improves policy enforcement even with a fixed archive. Updating the archive further reduces in-domain attack success compared with keeping it fixed. We compare policy-aware task agent self-regulation with a trained policy guard. On PolicyGym, the final guard-based configuration achieves a 40-44% relative reduction in attack success rate and fewer benign rejections than policy prompting alone.

AI.brief_summary: 提出 AgentPolicyForge 框架，用可执行环境构造策略基准 PolicyGym，并通过攻击者生成请求、环境执行核验的平衡样本迭代训练工具调用策略守卫。
AI.relevance_reason: 研究对象是外部工具调用的策略合规与守卫训练，不涉及视觉或多模态推理、内部 latent 状态、证据筛选或计算停止，其执行核验式标注也绑定具体工具环境，缺少可核查的 LVR 借鉴线索。
